item.title: Explicational statistics: research for an AI age
item.description: arXiv:2611.27961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI is dramatically changing the statistical research landscape. I argue that production of a distinct category of statistical knowledge, which I refer to as explicational statistics, is actually becoming more valuable as AI increasingly automates other parts of the research process. I define explicational statistics, contextualize it in terms of other forms of statistical knowledge, and explain why I think the rise of AI makes it more valuable. I demonstrate my framework by first developing a new dimension reduction method, Ambient Embedding Projection, that can simultaneously visualize the intrinsic geometry of a data manifold along with how that manifold is embedded into ambient space. I then use my new method to conceive of a new statistical property of a collection of manifolds, related to metric distortion, that in single-cell biology can capture the ensemble behavior of cell populations. I apply these ideas to single-nuclei RNA-seq data from the brains of mice from different behavioral conditions to reveal potential cellular mechanisms of chronic social defeat stress.
item.dc:creator: Sihai Dave Zhao

item.title: Longest run for $q$-binary trials
item.description: arXiv:2611.27828v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$. A simulation study confirms accurate maximum likelihood estimation of the base success probability and the geometric parameter $q$, a well-calibrated and powerful boundary-corrected likelihood ratio test of the hypothesis that $q=1$, and close agreement between the analytical cumulative distribution function and its empirical counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Jungtaek Oh, Nurzhan Sapargali

item.title: Deep Learning-based Approaches for State Space Models: A Selective Review
item.description: arXiv:2412.11211v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: State-space models (SSMs) offer a powerful framework for dynamical system analysis, wherein the temporal dynamics of the system are assumed to be captured through the evolution of the latent states, which govern the values of the observations. This paper provides a selective review of recent advancements in deep neural network-based approaches for SSMs, and presents a unified perspective for discrete-time deep state space models and continuous-time ones such as latent neural Ordinary Differential and Stochastic Differential Equations. It starts with an overview of the classical maximum likelihood based approach for learning SSMs, reviews the variational autoencoder as a general learning pipeline for neural network-based approaches in the presence of latent variables, and discusses in detail representative deep learning models that fall under the SSM framework. Very recent developments, where SSMs are used as standalone architectural modules for improving efficiency in sequence modeling, are also examined. Finally, we present examples involving nowcasting and irregularly sampled time-series data, together with a brief overview of scientific applications based on mechanistically structured SSMs.
item.dc:creator: Jiahe Lin, George Michailidis
